item.title: Manual Cervical Traction
clinicalUse: Selected compression-sensitive neck/radicular symptoms with clear favorable response
patientPosition: Supine with head comfortably supported and neck near neutral/slight flexion as tolerated.
stabilization: Therapist supports occiput and controls head throughout.
contact: Hands cradle occiput/suboccipital region without throat pressure.
forceDirection: Smooth longitudinal distraction along cervical axis.
Begin with very low force and increase only if symptoms improve.
dosage: Short test of 10–20 seconds; if helpful, repeat 3–5 times or use brief sustained bouts.
mistakes: Treating all radiculopathy automatically with traction.
safety: Avoid instability, fracture, severe myelopathy, suspected vascular pathology or progressive neurological loss.
item.visualCue: Occiput supported → smooth longitudinal distraction ↑ → monitor arm symptom response.

subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Short-term symptom modulation in selected neck/arm presentations
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supported sitting, supine or prone with the cervical spine relaxed.

subTechniques.direction: Smooth longitudinal distraction along cervical axis
subTechniques.dosage: Use a conservative response-guided trial and reassess before repeating.
